$comment: #1794 — the ONE policy for which ABI input fills activity_events.loan_id / offer_id. Read at runtime by packages/lib/src/activityRefs.ts (the indexer files rows by it; the app labels what it files) and by the guardrail (apps/indexer/scripts/lib/activity-refs-surface.mjs). Rationale for each section is in packages/lib/src/activityRefs.ts.

OfferMatched.offerId.why: #600 — a matcher fill calls acceptOfferInternal(borrowerOfferId), so the companion OfferAccepted already files the loan under the BORROWER offer; this event is the LENDER offer's only link to its matched child.

InternalMatchExecuted.loanId.why: Leg A is the canonical loan for the row; legs B and the optional C stay in args_json for clients that need the whole multi-leg payload.

LoanRefinanced.loanId.why: A refinance leaves two loan records. The new loan's own acceptance opens its timeline; this event is the old loan's closing transition and the only refinance-specific record on it. newLoanId stays in args_json.

RefinancePayoffSettled.loanId.why: #3042: the settlement statement of the old loan's payoff (what the new lender's net principal and the borrower's wallet each paid the old lender, and the borrower's treasury fee). It belongs on the old loan's timeline beside LoanRefinanced; newLoanId stays in args_json.

IntentMatched.offerId.why: The counterparty is the standing on-chain offer a person created and follows by offer id. The slice is a vehicle the protocol synthesizes inside this same transaction; its owner follows the intent by lender and asset pair, both in args_json.

SignedOfferMatched.offerId.why: Same rule as IntentMatched: the counterparty is the standing on-chain offer a person created; the slice is synthesized for the signed order, whose owner follows it by orderHash (in args_json).

LoanInitiatedDetails.loanId.why: Companion payload to LoanInitiated in the same transaction, which already carries the loan reference; scoping both would put the opening on the timeline twice.

OfferCreatedDetails.offerId.why: Companion payload to OfferCreated, which is offer-scoped already.

OfferCreatedDetails.loanId.why: Companion payload to OfferCreated. The only loan it names is the loan a refinance offer TARGETS, which nothing has happened to yet; the offer's own rows carry the offer reference.

OfferCanceledDetails.offerId.why: Companion payload to OfferCanceled, which is offer-scoped already.

SanctionedProceedsLocked.loanId.why: The input named loanId is not always a loan: on an offer-cancel refund it carries the OFFER id cast to uint256 (LibSanctionedLock), so filing the number under a loan could put the row on an unrelated loan. The recipient is in args_json.
